blocks.text: Gregor Mendel (1822-1884) studied inheritance in the garden pea, Pisum sativum. Peas were a good choice: they have many clearly contrasting characters (tall/dwarf, round/wrinkled seeds), a short generation time, many offspring, and their flowers normally self-pollinate, so Mendel could start with true-breeding lines and control every cross by hand.

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.text: Gene - a unit of inheritance found at a fixed position (locus) on a chromosome. Allele - one of the alternative forms of a gene, e.g. T (tall) and t (dwarf).

Each organism carries two alleles for a character, one from each parent. The two alleles separate (segregate) during gamete formation, so each gamete receives only one allele. At fertilisation the gametes fuse at random, restoring the pair.

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.text: Genotype - the alleles an organism carries for a character, e.g. TT, Tt or tt. Phenotype - the observable characteristic produced by the genotype together with the environment, e.g. tall or dwarf.

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.text: Homozygous - both alleles are the same (TT or tt). Heterozygous - the two alleles are different (Tt). A dominant allele (T) is expressed in the heterozygote; a recessive allele (t) is expressed only when homozygous.

items: P generation: tall TT x dwarf tt
Gametes: T from one parent, t from the other
F1: all Tt, all tall (tall is dominant)
F1 x F1: Tt x Tt gives 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt
F2 phenotypic ratio 3 tall : 1 dwarf; genotypic ratio 1 : 2 : 1

blocks.text: When two characters are followed together, the alleles of one gene separate into gametes independently of the alleles of the other gene. This happens because homologous chromosome pairs line up randomly at metaphase I of meiosis, so it applies to genes on different chromosomes (unlinked genes).

A plant heterozygous for seed shape (R round, r wrinkled) and seed colour (Y yellow, y green) makes four kinds of gametes in equal numbers: RY, Ry, rY and ry. Crossing two such plants gives 16 equally likely combinations.

blocks.title: Past-paper tip
blocks.text: 2021 Paper II: in structured questions on a dihybrid cross, marks are given for each step - parental genotypes, all four gamete types, a complete Punnett square and the 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio. Name the law (independent assortment) that explains the result.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text: Do not write the gametes of RrYy as Rr and Yy. A gamete carries ONE allele of each gene, e.g. RY.

items: Mendel used the garden pea, Pisum sativum: contrasting characters, self-pollination, many offspring.
Gene = unit of inheritance at a locus; alleles = alternative forms of a gene (T, t).
Genotype = alleles carried (TT, Tt, tt); phenotype = observable trait (tall, dwarf).
Homozygous = same alleles (TT, tt); heterozygous = different alleles (Tt).
A dominant allele shows in the heterozygote; a recessive allele only when homozygous.
Law of segregation: the two alleles separate during gamete formation, one per gamete.
Monohybrid F2 (Tt x Tt): 3 dominant : 1 recessive phenotype; 1 : 2 : 1 genotype.
Law of independent assortment: alleles of different genes assort independently (unlinked genes).
Cause: random orientation of homologous pairs at metaphase I of meiosis.
RrYy makes four gametes in equal numbers: RY, Ry, rY, ry.
Dihybrid F2 (RrYy x RrYy): 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 phenotypic ratio.
